answer: Random site presence attestation uses verified physical presence as the scarce resource. Each identity must, near dawn, photograph a one-time code at a randomly assigned public site. The registry accepts only images whose GPS, clock, and local steam plume texture match that site and rejects reused backgrounds. A pearl-sized color token in frame must also be unique per claim, so an attacker pays travel and time to capture fresh matched images at distinct sites for each identity.
